item.description: Researchers from Michigan State University and the University of Kentucky discovered that friendships with a shared identity are important for people in the LGBTQ+ community. item.title: Victoria bans unnecessary surgeries on intersex children
item.description: Intersex is a human trait that occurs as frequently as red hair or green eyes. According to sexologist Anne Fausto-Sterling, up to 1.7% of the world's population is born with chromosomal, hormonal or anatomical variations that deviate from typical definitions of male or female. item.title: Glow-worms return to Nosterfield after a century away
item.description: The glow-worm is making a comeback in North Yorkshire thanks to the unpaid work of nature enthusiast Peter Cooper. In his spare time, he breeds glow-worms in a garden shed and releases the larvae at Nosterfield Nature Reserve, where the creature has not been seen for a hundred years. Reserve manager Simon Warwick praised Cooper's „raw passion and enthusiasm". Nosterfield,...

item.title: Ban on dredging saves pink seaweed maerl at Summer Isles
item.description: A ban on industrial shellfish dredging introduced a decade ago has protected the magenta-coloured seaweed species maerl around the Summer Isles in Scotland. Maerl forms hard, chalky nodules on the seabed and provides habitat for fish. item.description: A high school student from New Jersey, Shashank Madala, witnessed adults misinterpreting the emotional signals of his autistic cousin during family gatherings. At fifteen, with just one computer science class under his belt, he taught himself machine learning and built the free app Kora. item.title: Mayor catches stone thief with AirTag in Rufford
item.description: An English mayor, Matt Smith, solved a theft himself after police in the Lancashire village of Rufford could not help due to lack of camera footage. From May onwards, stones were stolen from a 300-year-old wall, with an estimated value of around $9,000. item.title: Escaped parakeet Luna found in drain after motorist's tip
item.description: A parakeet named Luna has been reunited with her owner after flying away when storm Boelo blew open a kitchen window in Northampton, England. A passing motorist spotted the little bird hopping in a roadside drain and alerted the RSPCA. Inspector Richard Durant and trainee Rosie Cowie attended the scene and found Luna's beak, chirping from a pipe in the...

item.title: Karl Bushby embraces mother after 28 years walking around the world
item.description: British adventurer Karl Bushby has returned to his birthplace Hull after 28 years, where he embraced his tearful mother Angela. The former parachutist set out in 1998 on a 31,000-mile journey through 30 countries, entirely on foot. item.title: World buys Rothbury Estate for nature restoration
item.description: The Rothbury Estate in Northumberland, owned by the Dukes of Northumberland for 800 years since the 13th century, has been purchased by the Wildlife Trusts. More than 25,000 donors from 50 countries raised £30 million together for the 9,400-hectare estate. It will become part of a 40-mile nature corridor between Druridge Bay and an existing nature reserve. The estate is...

item.title: From homeless to Oscar: the story behind Rocky and Sylvester Stallone
item.description: In the nineteen seventies, Sylvester Stallone was homeless in New York and worked long days filleting fish, while audition after audition fell through. His ambition to become an actor was not taken seriously, partly due to partial facial paralysis and a speech impediment resulting from a difficult birth. item.title: Satish Kumar wins Future Icons Award for 8,000-mile peace walk
item.description: Country & Town House has announced the winners of the Future Icons Awards 2027 and the Future Icons Power List 2027. Satish Kumar, founder of the Resurgence Trust which publishes The Ecologist, was honoured for walking 8,000 miles through 15 countries in the 1960s without money for peace and for founding Schumacher College in 1991. item.title: European Innovation Council receives €1.8 billion for 2027
item.description: The European Commission has announced €1.8 billion in funding for 2027 through the European Innovation Council (EIC). With this budget, the Commission aims to accelerate the development of breakthrough technologies and support ambitious startups. The goal is to strengthen Europe's position in the global innovation race.

item.title: Vermont Gas brings geothermal heating to affordable homes
item.description: Vermont Gas has struck a groundbreaking deal with geothermal developer Dandelion Energy to equip the 44-unit affordable housing project Riggs Meadow in Hinesburg with geothermal heating and cooling. item.title: Toxic Bangka loris turns out not to have gone extinct after all
item.description: The Bangka slow loris, a primate that had not been scientifically observed since the 1930s and was considered possibly extinct in 2015, has apparently survived all along. Austrian scientists discovered this thanks to a 2022 field guide that referenced the Alobi Wildlife Rescue Center on the island of Bangka. This center has been rescuing and reintroducing the animals since 2015,...

item.title: Solar kits transform disaster relief
item.description: Solar kits are bringing a new approach to disaster relief. According to The Optimist Daily, this form of solar energy is changing the way aid is organized and delivered after disasters.

item.title: Erik's Ranch in Montana: autistic guides and wranglers welcome guests
item.description: At Erik's Ranch & Retreats in Montana, near Yellowstone National Park, autistic people work as concierges, guides, wranglers and cooks. Many of them also live on the 230-hectare property. Founder Kathryn Nordberg started the initiative in 2014 out of concern for the future of her autistic son Erik. The cabins are specially designed for neurodivergent guests: calm colors, soundproof doors...

item.description: Researchers at Northeastern University are looking to butterflies to develop safer paint and glitter without harmful chemical pigments. They are investigating 'structural colour', where microscopic structures reflect light, as seen in butterfly wings and peacock feathers. item.description: Early November shows that science doesn't only happen in laboratories, but also comes to life in unexpected places. item.title: Open Research Europe expands free publishing to 11 countries
item.description: Researchers from 11 European countries can now publish free of charge via Open Research Europe (ORE), the European Commission's open access platform. This follows an expansion of the initiative, giving more scientists in Europe access to publishing without having to pay publication fees.

item.title: Great Terns Return to British South Coast After Bird Flu
item.description: Thanks to targeted nature conservation, great terns have reclaimed a colony on England's south coast, three years after bird flu wiped out the population entirely. Little terns, ringed plovers, common terns and oystercatchers also increased in numbers thanks to the same conservation work by the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB). item.title: Personalized brain therapy achieves 68 percent remission in PTSD
item.description: A personalized form of brain therapy results in remission for 68 percent of people with PTSD. This figure is cited in a report from The Optimist Daily, though further details about the precise mechanism, study design, or researchers involved are lacking. The news is presented as a positive development in mental health care and technology.

item.title: Brazil's Pantanal National Park Significantly Expanded
item.description: Brazilian environmental authorities have expanded the Pantanal Matogrossense National Park by more than 25%: from 523 square miles to 185 additional square miles, roughly equivalent to adding the American Redwoods National Park. The expansion protects the Pantanal, the world's largest flooded grasslands and one of the richest and most vulnerable biomes on Earth. It is home to 463 bird species,...

item.description: Filmmaker Ora DeKornfeld made the documentary The Grandfather Puzzle to get closer to her 99-year-old grandfather, who never wanted to talk about his life in Hungary as a baron. item.title: Catherine Breed becomes first to swim entire California coast
item.description: Long-distance swimmer Catherine Breed is the first person to swim the entire California coastline: 900 miles in 111 days. She started on July 1 at the Oregon-California border and completed the journey on October 19, passing the Mexico border roughly 3 miles offshore to avoid pollution from the Tijuana River. item.description: An auto repair shop run by students has opened in Houston's Fifth Ward. item.description: Maha Khan, a master's student in food security at the University of Reading, has created a chocolate bar made entirely from British ingredients, including the cocoa beans themselves.
